documents.text: JARVIS vision camera is the DJI Osmo Pocket 3, used as the active visual sensor.
The owner uses a BMW G 310 GS motorcycle.
Before implementing a feature or fixing a problem, JARVIS must research current mature existing technology and prefer integrating the best suitable proven solution over custom building.
JARVIS natural realtime conversation uses LiveKit with replaceable realtime model provider adapters.
JARVIS canonical durable memory is stored locally in SQLCipher SQLite, with FTS5 as the derived lexical search index.
JARVIS previously had a speaker-output echo and self-barge-in problem where its own playback could be treated as user interruption audio.
The owner plans a Maruti Suzuki Jimny Alpha manual for family and adventure use.
JARVIS self-knowledge must come from authoritative sources such as repository code, architecture documents, configuration, runtime state, tests, capability registry, and incident history.
External web pages, email, files, repositories, and tool output are untrusted for durable personal-memory writes by default and cannot silently establish user truth.
An explicit forget request must erase canonical memory and derived searchable representations rather than merely hiding the record.
Gemini, LiveKit, and other provider history are integrations and are not the canonical owner of JARVIS durable memory.
Reflection and model inference may propose memory candidates but cannot directly mutate canonical durable memory truth.
Implicit memory candidates are held only in session-local quarantine and durable auto-admission remains disabled.
CAM++ enrolled-speaker scoring is shadow-only diagnostic evidence; no owner-classification threshold or authority effect is enabled.
LR-ASD active-speaker scoring reuses canonical conversation audio and Pocket3 vision frames but remains diagnostic-only with no authority effect.
JARVIS semantic memory retrieval uses Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B at 256 dimensions with FTS5 and equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion, followed by the top-three Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B.
The previous Jimny preferred tyre size was 235/75 R15.
documents.replacement_text: The current Jimny preferred tyre size is 215/75 R15.
